title: Learning Model Demos
one_liner: Interactive browser demos of classic associative learning models, from Rescorla-Wagner through Mackintosh, Pearce-Hall, and Wagner's SOP to MINERVA-AL, built so students can read each equation, watch it run, and see which term produces which behaviour.
description:
## What

Example demos that show how learning models work. They begin with classic models such as Rescorla-Wagner and Mackintosh and build toward MINERVA-AL, the instance-based model of associative learning.

## Why

Learning models are much easier to understand when you can run them. Watching associative strength change trial by trial makes each model's assumptions concrete. Running the same training design through several models shows where they agree and where they make different predictions. Ending with MINERVA-AL shows how an instance-based account handles the same phenomena in a different way.

## How

Early thoughts, to refine in a workshop:

- **A sequence of models.** Rescorla-Wagner first, then the attention models of Mackintosh and Pearce-Hall, then Wagner's real-time SOP model, and then MINERVA-AL. A configural model and AESOP can come later.
- **Interactive in the browser.** Each demo lets people set learning parameters, design a sequence of trials, run it, and watch the predictions change over trials on a chart.
- **Classic phenomena as presets.** Acquisition, extinction, blocking, overshadowing, conditioned inhibition, latent inhibition, backward blocking, and negative patterning. Several of these are exactly where the models part ways, which makes them good teaching cases.
- **Side by side.** Run one design through two or more models at once to compare their predictions directly.
- **Teach the equations, not just show them.** Each equation can be read as words, symbols, live numbers for the selected trial, or code. Symbols are colour-linked to sliders, chart lines, and a hand-calculation trial table. A build-the-equation mode adds one term at a time and shows which phenomenon each term unlocks, and assumption toggles remove one assumption while everything else stays fixed. A primer page teaches how to read the notation.
- **Simple to host.** A static site in plain HTML and JavaScript with no build step, served from GitHub Pages first and mirrored on Coolify or the lab website later. Matching R or Quarto versions could support course materials.
- **Connections.** Useful for teaching and for classroom demos on the Open Psychology Platform. A good example of how computational models make predictions explicit, the theme of the theory-evaluation idea. A lead-in to the instance theory work, including the ITS experiments.
open_questions: Confirm or change the plan's defaults: courses first; Rescorla-Wagner, Mackintosh, Pearce-Hall, SOP, and MINERVA-AL in that order; a static site on GitHub Pages first with Coolify later; the instance theory of semantics as a later extension.
Which course or courses will use the demos first, and when? This sets the deadline for Milestone 1 and the student try-out at its end.
Which explicit version of Mackintosh's associability rule to use, since the 1975 paper gives only the direction of the change.
notes:
- 2026-10-03: Captured from chat as a seed. The user wants example demos of how learning models work, such as the classic Rescorla-Wagner and Mackintosh models, leading up to MINERVA-AL.
- 2026-10-03: Transcription notes: "Rescorla-Wegener" was recorded as Rescorla-Wagner, "Macintosh" as Mackintosh, and "Minerva AL" as MINERVA-AL. Correct these if wrong.
- 2026-10-04: Plan written to plan.md at the user's request without a question round. The open questions were settled with stated defaults: courses first; Rescorla-Wagner, Mackintosh, Pearce-Hall, and MINERVA-AL as the first models; plain HTML and JavaScript demos with no build step; a new repo deployed on Coolify; the instance theory of semantics as a later extension. Each model is verified against published results in automated tests before classroom use.
- 2026-10-04: Plan revised. A static site on GitHub Pages is now the first deliverable, with Coolify, R, and Quarto later. Wagner's SOP model added as the fourth model, before MINERVA-AL, which adds time within a trial to the design format and model interface. The plan is reorganized around three student difficulties: reading a formula, connecting the formula to the model's behaviour, and seeing its implications. Every model page now has an equation panel with words, symbols, live numbers, and code readings, an arithmetic view, a hand-calculation trial table, step controls, a build-the-equation mode, assumption toggles, predict-first sketching, phenomenon cards, and share links, plus a primer page on reading equations.
- 2026-10-04: Milestone 1 built: the static site skeleton and the Rescorla-Wagner page with all the teaching views in the plan. Still open for Milestone 1: turning on GitHub Pages after merge, and a try-out with students.
- 2026-10-04: Students tried the Rescorla-Wagner page, liked it, and asked for more scaffolding. Milestone 2 built in response: a primer on reading the equations with live widgets, check-yourself questions, worked fixed points checked against the model, and a notation map; predict-first sketching on the model page; and a how-to-use guide and primer links on the model page.
